one_liner: Senior Executive who runs the Education Department's small business office, setting goals and policy so small and disadvantaged firms win more ED contracts.
fit_summary: This SES role requires executive leadership across all five ECQs plus experience leading a small business or federal acquisition program under the FAR. Daniel knows the contractor side of federal acquisition from finding opportunities and leading proposal writing at IEM, but his resume shows no executive leadership or program management at this level, so skip it.
eligibility: Open to the public (hiring paths include public and SES), so no federal status is needed; U.S. citizenship is required.
The two-page resume itself must show all five ECQs and both TQs; failing to address any one means disqualification, and separate narratives are not accepted.
TQ 1 requires demonstrated experience leading a small business utilization or federal acquisition program, and TQ 2 requires applying the FAR and small business contracting rules.
You must obtain a Public Trust clearance, file an OGE-278 financial disclosure, and receive OPM QRB approval before appointment.
The application window runs from October 23 to November 6, 2026.
strategy: Skip this one: this SES role requires executive leadership plus experience leading a small business or federal acquisition program under the FAR, and his resume shows neither.
His proposal and procurement work fits GS-9 Contract Specialist (1102) or GS-0301 program roles, which build FAR experience.
resume_bullets: Found contract opportunities in SAM.gov, GovWin and BidPro and led proposal writing for multimillion-dollar bids (2019–2024).
Worked with medical supply, truck rental and other vendors for COVID-19 sites (2021–2022).
interview_questions: How have you used the FAR to develop an acquisition strategy that increased small business participation?
Describe how you would negotiate annual socioeconomic goals with SBA and with ED's two procurement offices.
Tell us about a time you led a team through change and held people accountable for results.
How would you use data-based metrics to show whether OSDBU is meeting its targets?
watch_outs: SES-level requirements, including executive leadership and direct small business or acquisition program experience, likely exceed your documented background, and OPM QRB approval is an added hurdle.
The job is based in DC with telework eligibility, but it is not remote, the position may be detailed to another agency, and relocation is not paid.
